note:
Class 6B, week of 16 November. Notes for myself.

Aarav Sharma has missed four days this month. His mother Sunita told me on the phone (98765 43210) that his father lost his job at the mill and the family cannot pay for anything extra this term; Aarav now helps at the family tea stall before school. He is bright in maths but has not handed in homework for two weeks.

Meenal reads well aloud but freezes in written tests. She needs extra writing practice, and the remedial writing club meets after the last bell. She told me she has epilepsy and is afraid of having a seizure in the exam hall. Her roll no. 6B/23. She walks six kilometres home to Rampur Kalan and has to leave school at the last bell to reach home before dark.

Kabir and Ishaan fight most days during group work. Kabir's parents are separating and he is staying with his grandmother. Ishaan finishes early and gets bored.

Tanvi is far ahead in reading. She could help others, but she is shy. Her family does not have a smartphone or an internet connection. Every Tuesday she goes with her grandmother to the town clinic and has to miss school that day, and her mother cooks in two homes until evening.

Lesson
Class: Class 6
Subject: English
Topic: Writing a short description of a place
Length: 40 minutes

draft.title: Class 6 English — Writing a Short Description of a Place

items.heading: Starter (5 minutes)
items.text: Say to the class: Close your eyes and think of your favourite place in your town or village, like the park or the market. Write on the chalkboard the heading: My Favourite Place. Ask pupils to open their notebooks and write down three things they can see in that place.

items.heading: Teach (10 minutes)
items.text: Say to the class: A good description uses words that help the reader see, hear, and feel the place. Write on the chalkboard the following model paragraph: The old village well is a busy spot in the morning. Cool water sparkles in the sunlight as women fill their brass pots. Children laugh and run around the large neem tree nearby. Write on the chalkboard: Use colour words and sound words to bring your place alive.

items.heading: Practise (15 minutes)
items.text: Say to the class: Now write five sentences describing your chosen place in your notebooks using the chalkboard model as a guide. Write on the chalkboard: Include what you see, what you hear, and how it feels. Walk around the classroom with chalk and pens to assist pupils as they write.

items.heading: Check (10 minutes)
items.text: Say to the class: Exchange your notebook with your seatmate and read their description quietly. Ask pupils to check if their partner used at least one colour word and one sound word. Ask volunteers to stand up and read one good sentence from their partner's work to the class.

items.heading: Homework
items.text: Say to the class: Copy your corrected paragraph neatly into the back of your notebook for practice. Write on the chalkboard: Homework: Write three more sentences describing what happens at your place in the evening.
